channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Tyler Goodson rushed seven times for 14 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona, adding two catches for 19 yards on his only two targets.
item.description: He found 20-of-74 running back snaps against the Cardinals; not bad work but nothing that is making you consider a waiver claim either. Goodson should be held in deeper leagues as a contingency stash.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Braelon Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Omar Cooper Jr. was not targeted in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Chase Brown rushed 12 times for 55 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding 8 receptions for 46 yards.
item.description: Brown saw most of his fantasy production come from the passing game, seeing nine targets in a pass-heavy game script. He fumbled on a handoff from Joe Burrow and also had a receiving touchdown called back for holding in the first half. Despite the dampened fantasy production, Brown saw most of the backfield opportunities for the Bengals, out-touching Samaje Perine 20-to-5. Brown’s production has been underwhelming the first half of the season but fantasy managers should hold tight given his large share of opportunities in pass-heavy game scripts. Brown’s production should regress to see more touchdowns the second half of the season. He is in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Javonte Williams rushed 24 times for 56 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description: Woof. The Cardinals simply overwhelmed the line of scrimmage with run blitzes and dared the Cowboys to do something about it; they often didn’t. Williams also fumbled away a goal-line tote only for it to wind up as a Cowboys touchdown by landing in the hands of journeyman tight end James Mitchell. Things should be easier next week against the Colts, where Williams will remain a reasonable RB1/high-end RB2 tweener.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Cade Otton was not targeted in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
item.description: Otton has one catch over his past three appearances and hasn’t hit 40 yards since Week 3. The Bucs, who only attempted three passes today, will increase the pass volume in Week 9, but that alone won’t be enough to get Otton back into fantasy lineups. He is not even in the TE2 mix for Week 9 against the Bears.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Jordan Addison caught 3-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
item.description: Kyler Murray targeted Addison deep a few times in this one and connected with Addison on a 51-yard deep shot over double coverage in the injury-riddled Lions secondary. It was good to see signs of life from Addison, who entered Week 8 averaging fewer expected fantasy points per game than Cooper Kupp and Kendrick Bourne. The team’s primary downfield threat, Addison’s role in the run-heavy Minnesota offense makes him a boom-bust weekly play. That won’t change in a good matchup in Week 9 against the Bills.-Denny Carter

item.title: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ 33-30, Week 8 loss to the Cardinals, adding seven carries for 20 yards and a touchdown on the ground.
item.description: If you’re wondering, it was Prescott’s first rushing touchdown since Week 12 of the 2025 season against the Eagles, and his first game with seven carries since Week 5 of the 2025 season. The gist of it is: The Cardinals big blitzed a lot and vacated several underneath zones to allow Prescott to run. Dallas often tried to solve things pre-snap, and they often did — but not often enough to win. Dallas was either throwing haymakers or quickly finding themselves going three-and-out, as they did in overtime. Prescott will get to rebound quickly in Week 9 against a Colts outfit that barely qualifies as a serious football team amid what has the look of a fire sale.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Trevor Lawrence completed 10-of-14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 42-7, Week 8 win over the Colts, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
item.description: This came in only three quarters of work, as Lawrence spent the fourth frame on the bench with the Jags demolishing the quitting Colts. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, early breathers have been a theme for Lawrence this season as his well-rounded team keeps blowing out less impressive sides. Rather unbelievably, that could now include the Ravens for Week 9, as Baltimore appears down to its No. 3 quarterback for the sides’ short-week Thursday night tilt. That won’t be enough to force Lawrence out of starting lineups, but he can’t be expected to single-handedly win matchups in that environment.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Ted Hurst failed to catch his only target in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
item.description: Baker Mayfield only attempted three passes in this game. One of them was a deep shot for Hurst into the end zone. Hurst initially had the catch as he spun around for the back-shoulder ball, but Falcons corner Mike Hughes jarred the ball loose for an incompletion. It was Hurst’s second week in a row with zero catches on one target. Hurst has topped out at three catches for 40 yards in a single game this year. He isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 9.-Kyle Dvorchak
